 | 4 | 2 | 8 | 9 | 6 | 3 | 1 | 7 | 5 | 
 | 3 | 7 | 9 | 5 | 2 | 1 | 6 | 8 | 4 | 
 | 5 | 6 | 1 | 8 | 4 | 7 | 9 | 2 | 3 | 
 The number of different ways to fill such a grid can be written as $p^a\cdot q^b\cdot r^c\cdot s^d$, where $p,q,r,$ and $s$ are distinct prime numbers and $a,b,c,$ and $d$ are positive integers. Find $p\cdot a+q\cdot b+r\cdot c+s\cdot d$.

labeled_steps.reasoning_step: We view the 3×9 band as three 3×3 blocks (columns 1–3, 4–6, 7–9). Each symbol 1,…,9 must appear once in each row and once in each block; hence for each symbol s its three occurrences give a permutation π_s ∈ S3 (π_s(j) = the row in which s appears inside block j). Thus we must choose nine permutations (with repetition) so that for each block j and each row r exactly 3 symbols satisfy π_s(j)=r.

Let x_π be how many symbols are assigned permutation π. Index the 6 permutations of S3 as e,(12),(13),(23),(123),(132) with counts a,b,c,d,e′,f. For each block j and row r the sum of the two x_π for permutations sending j→r must be 3. Solving these linear equations gives the family of integer solutions
(a,b,c,d,e′,f) = (t,3−t,3−t,3−t,t,t) for t = 0,1,2,3.

labeled_steps.reasoning_step:
For a fixed t the number of ways to choose which of the 9 distinct symbols get which permutation is the multinomial
9!/(a! b! c! d! e′! f!) = 9!/(t!^3 (3−t)!^3).
Summing over t = 0,…,3 gives the number of assignments of permutations to symbols:
S = sum_{t=0}^3 9!/(t!^3 (3−t)!^3) = 94080.
